claim_verdicts.claim_text: Spironolactone was taken daily from 2026-02-19 and potassium rose to 5.7 mmol/L on 2026-03-02

citations.quote: started by outpatient cardiology on 2026-02-19 and taken daily since

claim_verdicts.why: Both facts are documented, and spironolactone exposure did precede the initial rise, so it is a plausible contributor.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The Day 4 note confirms the hyperkalemia was secondary to spironolactone
claim_verdicts.why: The Day 4 note says 'likely', not 'confirmed', and it addresses the second episode after the drug was resumed, not the initial onset.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: Spironolactone is the cause of the initial elevation

citations.quote: differential includes reduced renal potassium clearance, ACE inhibitor effect and recent spironolactone use

claim_verdicts.why: Spironolactone is plausible but unproven: the treating note left the cause open, with acute kidney injury and lisinopril as competing explanations.

explanation: Spironolactone can plausibly have contributed to the initial potassium rise: it was taken daily from 2026-02-19 through the morning of admission. But the record does not establish it as the cause. The Day 2 note said the etiology was not yet clear, listing acute kidney injury and lisinopril (given 03-01) alongside spironolactone. The answer leans on the Day 4 note, but that note only says 'likely' and concerns the later rise after spironolactone was resumed on 03-03, not the initial onset. The answer states causation definitively and never says what remains unknown.
